meta.title: Foundations of Linear Algebra for Machine Learning
meta.target_outcome: Build the linear algebra foundation needed to read and implement ML papers confidently.
meta.current_level: Comfortable with high-school algebra; no prior linear algebra.
meta.notes: This is a small worked example demonstrating the schema, not a complete curriculum. Field values are illustrative.

modules.title: Vectors, Vector Spaces, and Linear Combinations
learning_objectives: Define vectors, vector spaces, and subspaces
Compute linear combinations and determine linear independence by hand
Explain span and basis both geometrically and algebraically
deep_understanding_concepts: Why linear independence guarantees a unique representation in a given basis
The relationship between span, basis, and dimension
common_mistakes: Treating vectors purely as lists of numbers without geometric intuition
Confusing 'spans the space' with 'is a basis for the space'
modules.expected_competence: Can determine whether a given set of vectors is linearly independent and/or spans a given space, and justify the answer without a calculator.
modules.industry_expectations: Assumed fluent background for any ML, quant, or scientific computing role; gaps here surface as confusion in later derivations.
mastery_goals: Reason about vector spaces abstractly enough to follow proofs in later modules

evaluation.description: Solve a problem set on independence, span, and basis, including at least two short proofs of linear (in)dependence.
Explain, without notes, why a basis is the minimal spanning set and why dimension is well-defined.

real_world_competence: Recognizing when a feature matrix has linearly dependent columns (multicollinearity) and what that implies for downstream models

resources.title: Introductory linear algebra textbook or course covering vector spaces, span, and basis
resources.notes: No resource specified yet -- ask the user what they have access to before recommending anything.

modules.title: Matrix Operations and Linear Transformations
learning_objectives: Perform matrix addition, multiplication, and inversion by hand for small matrices
Interpret a matrix as a linear transformation between vector spaces
Compute and interpret rank, null space, and column space
deep_understanding_concepts: Matrix multiplication as composition of linear transformations, not just a row-by-column algorithm
Why rank-nullity ties together the dimensions of domain, range, and kernel
common_mistakes: Memorizing the multiplication algorithm without connecting it to function composition
modules.expected_competence: Can compute rank, null space, and column space for a 3x3 or 4x4 matrix by hand, and explain what each tells you about the corresponding linear transformation.
modules.industry_expectations: Used daily in any role involving linear models, computer graphics, optimization, or numerical methods.
mastery_goals: Read matrix-based derivations in papers without needing to re-derive multiplication rules

evaluation.description: Compute rank, null space, and column space for a set of matrices, including at least one rank-deficient example.
Implement matrix multiplication and Gaussian elimination from scratch (no library calls) and validate against a library implementation.

real_world_competence: Debugging a numerical pipeline where a matrix is unexpectedly singular or near-singular
Understanding why floating-point matrix operations can be numerically unstable for ill-conditioned matrices

resources.title: Same primary resource as the previous module, chapters on matrix operations and linear transformations
resources.notes: Depends on the resource selected for vectors-and-spaces.

modules.title: Matrix Decompositions (LU, QR, SVD)
learning_objectives: Explain what LU, QR, and SVD decompositions represent geometrically
Choose an appropriate decomposition for a given numerical problem
deep_understanding_concepts: SVD as the generalization of eigendecomposition to non-square matrices
Why decompositions improve numerical stability compared to direct methods
common_mistakes: Treating decompositions as black-box library calls without understanding what they reveal about the matrix
modules.expected_competence: Can explain what each decomposition reveals about a matrix (rank, conditioning, principal directions) and pick the right one for a stated numerical problem.
modules.industry_expectations: SVD in particular underlies PCA, recommender systems, and many dimensionality-reduction techniques used in production ML systems.
mastery_goals: Connect SVD to PCA before starting any applied ML modules

evaluation.description: Implement PCA via SVD on a small dataset and verify the result matches a library implementation.

real_world_competence: Recognizing when SVD-based dimensionality reduction is discarding meaningful signal vs. noise

resources.title: Same primary resource, chapter on matrix decompositions
resources.notes: This submodule is optional; can be deferred if time-constrained.

modules.notes: This is a submodule of matrix-operations. It is optional and can be skipped on a first pass.

modules.title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and Diagonalization
learning_objectives: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors for small matrices by hand
Diagonalize a matrix when possible and explain when it is not possible
Connect eigendecomposition to repeated linear transformations
deep_understanding_concepts: Eigenvectors as directions preserved (up to scaling) by a transformation
Why not all matrices are diagonalizable, and what that implies practically
common_mistakes: Computing eigenvalues correctly but failing to interpret what they mean for the underlying transformation
Assuming all square matrices are diagonalizable
modules.expected_competence: Can compute eigenvalues/eigenvectors for a 3x3 matrix by hand, diagonalize it if possible, and explain the geometric meaning of the result.
modules.industry_expectations: Foundational for PCA, spectral clustering, stability analysis of dynamical systems, and convergence analysis of iterative algorithms.
mastery_goals: Be able to read and follow the spectral-theory sections of an ML or optimization paper without external help

evaluation.description: Compute eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalizations for a set of matrices, including at least one non-diagonalizable example.
Derive the power iteration method for finding the dominant eigenvector and explain its convergence condition.

real_world_competence: Diagnosing why an iterative algorithm fails to converge by examining the spectral radius of its update matrix

resources.title: Same primary resource, chapters on eigenvalues and diagonalization

modules.notes: Marked as not skippable: this module is foundational enough that even learners with prior exposure should validate it explicitly.

modules.title: Introduction to Vector Calculus (Gradients and Jacobians)
learning_objectives: Compute gradients and Jacobians for multivariate functions
Explain the geometric meaning of the gradient as the direction of steepest ascent
deep_understanding_concepts: The Jacobian as a local linear approximation of a nonlinear map
common_mistakes: Confusing the gradient (a vector) with the derivative (a scalar) when generalizing from single-variable calculus
modules.expected_competence: Can compute the gradient and Jacobian of a given multivariate function and explain what each represents geometrically.
modules.industry_expectations: Directly underlies gradient descent and backpropagation; expected baseline for any ML engineering role.
mastery_goals: Be ready to study gradient-based optimization without first needing a calculus refresher

evaluation.description: Compute gradients and Jacobians for a set of multivariate functions by hand.

real_world_competence: Recognizing exploding/vanishing gradient symptoms as a Jacobian-conditioning problem

resources.title: Any standard multivariable calculus reference covering gradients and Jacobians
resources.notes: This module runs in parallel with matrix-operations -- it shares only the vectors-and-spaces prerequisite.

modules.notes: Optional and parallel: useful before any ML-application module, but not required to proceed through the core linear algebra sequence.

modules.title: Milestone Project: PCA and Linear Regression from Scratch
learning_objectives: Implement PCA from scratch using eigendecomposition or SVD
Implement ordinary least squares linear regression from scratch using matrix operations
Explain how each algorithm depends on the linear algebra concepts covered in this roadmap
deep_understanding_concepts: How the normal equations for linear regression arise from a least-squares minimization in vector-space terms
common_mistakes: Implementing PCA/regression by calling library functions without being able to explain the underlying linear algebra
modules.expected_competence: Can implement both algorithms from scratch, explain every linear-algebra step used, and correctly diagnose failures (e.g., singular matrices) on edge-case inputs.
modules.industry_expectations: Being able to implement and explain these from first principles is a common bar in ML interviews and is directly useful when debugging library behavior in production.
mastery_goals: Demonstrate end-to-end mastery of the linear algebra foundation by applying it to two canonical ML algorithms

evaluation.description: Build a small project implementing PCA and OLS linear regression from scratch (no high-level ML libraries), tested on a real dataset, with a short write-up explaining each linear-algebra step.
Given a deliberately ill-conditioned dataset, diagnose why the from-scratch regression implementation produces unstable coefficients and propose a fix.

real_world_competence: Handling a near-singular design matrix in linear regression (multicollinearity) using regularization or dimensionality reduction
Explaining trade-offs between implementing from scratch vs. using optimized library routines in production

resources.title: Any small tabular dataset suitable for linear regression and PCA
resources.notes: User should supply or choose a dataset; not specified here.
